rationale: Second finding on hashicorp/raft startup: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs before NewRaft starts the FSM goroutine, so a committed backlog larger than the 128-slot FSM queue can never be drained and NewRaft never returns. Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the violation: the above-buffer case emitted newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait with 8402 committed entries and no snapshot, so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The control comparison came back unknown only because both backlog cases shared one result event name, which made the controller look for the other case's admission under each comparison; its event still shows newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries. The corrected declaration splits the result event names per case and is submitted as a successor experiment so the control can complete. The configuration-loss question stays as previously recorded and is not restated here.

investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied before the startup configuration scan, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below the restored commit index are skipped and the node keeps the snapshot (or empty) configuration.
investigations.discriminator: Restart identical stores with the flag on and off and compare configuration index, server count and hasVote immediately after NewRaft returns; then repeat with a snapshot older than a committed configuration change.

investigations.question: Does a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and a large committed backlog complete, given that restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs before the FSM goroutine is started?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch into fsmMutateCh, whose capacity is 128, while runFSM is only started after NewRaft returns; a backlog requiring more than 128 batches blocks NewRaft forever.
investigations.discriminator: Commit N committed entries with no snapshot and restart: a backlog whose batch count is below the queue capacity returns promptly, while a slightly larger one never returns within a bounded wait.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, NewRaft replays the committed log by pushing one fsmMutateCh message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch before the FSM goroutine is started; when the committed backlog requires more batches than the queue's 128 slots the send blocks and NewRaft never returns, so the node never starts.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot covering the committed range, and a restored commit index whose replay needs more than 128 batches of MaxAppendEntries entries (default 64, about 8192 entries); observed for 8402 entries (132 batches) with a bounded 15 second wait, against 8002 entries (126 batches) returning in 0-3 ms.

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the prediction: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot, 8402 committed entries and a restored commit index of 8402 (event index 8), the restart reported newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait (event index 9), so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The paired below-capacity case is retained as an observation, not as a completed comparison: event index 7 reports newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries, but comparison 1 returned unknown because both backlog cases shared one result event name, so each comparison looked for the other case's admission and the controller marked the other result incomplete; the corrected declaration gives each size its own result event and is submitted as a successor experiment. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A replay needing more than 128 batches therefore blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft, with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence under the stated conditions: the node never finishes starting, so a node that should resume service after a restart does not, and every duty depending on it (elections, replication, convergence) is stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 the boundary sits near 8192 committed entries and the default TrailingLogs of 10240 allows a log that large before any snapshot.
counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returned immediately (0 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness of replaying committed logs.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded 15 second wait, not an infinite-run proof; a different schedule or a later repair is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size are taken from the source, not measured.
The configuration-loss finding under the parent question is a separate defect and is not part of this account.

experiment.revision_reason: Only the comparison declaration and the per-case result event names change: each backlog size now emits its own result event (restart_backlog_below / restart_backlog_above) so each comparison sees exactly one result event and can complete. Inputs, sizes, bounded wait and assertions are unchanged.

scope.description: Boot one node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and a CommitTrackingLogStore, commit 8000 and then (separately) 8400 entries without any snapshot, restart from the same stores, and report whether NewRaft returns within a bounded 15 second wait.
assumptions: MaxAppendEntries keeps its default of 64, so 8002 committed entries need 126 batches while 8402 need 132.
No snapshot is taken, so restoreFromCommittedLogs replays the whole committed log.
The two sizes bracket the FSM queue capacity without changing any production logic.
excluded: Any judgment about how long a large but sub-capacity replay may legitimately take.
The configuration-loss finding, recorded under the parent question.

experiment.prefix: The harness uses the package's own test facilities (inmemConfig, MakeClusterOpts with CommitTrackingLogs, MakeClusterCustom), commits the entries through Apply, shuts the node down, then calls NewRaft on a separate goroutine so the test can report a bounded wait. Each case emits a startup_before_restart event and then its own result event (restart_backlog_below or restart_backlog_above) carrying newraft_returned, restart_wait_ms and the same operands; no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns startup: NewRaft must either return or fail, and must not depend on a component it starts only after returning.

comparisons.description: With a committed backlog needing more batches than the FSM queue holds, NewRaft is expected to return; the defect prediction is that it never returns.
Control: with a backlog staying below the queue capacity NewRaft is expected to return, separating the queue-capacity mechanism from a generally slow replay.
